newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower, waiting on election news.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower, waiting on election news.

text.p: French shares finished with a big loss on Monday as political risk stalked the markets.

Traders said the market was waiting for confirmation that President Jacques Chirac would dissolve parliament and set a parliamentary election date, either in late May or early June, in a televised address on Monday night.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 24.89 points or 0.98 percent at 2,522.67, off its session lows. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 22 at 2,522 from Friday's close.
Volume was a moderate 5.5 billion francs.
The franc weakened, trading at 3.3755 per mark compared to late Friday's 3.3698. The June 10-year bond future contract settled down 0.44 at 128.28.

Although the markets are expected to be volatile in the next few weeks, some analysts are banking on a return of the centre-right to boost chances that France will take the measures needed to join the euro on time.

Some see a target of 2,800 for the CAC index in the medium-term if the ruling coalition wins. And if there are no clear trends from opinion polls in the election run-up, the CAC could come back to 2,400-2,450 before bottoming out.
The psychological 2,500 level held up today, giving hopes the market could rise on Tuesday -- if Chirac gives a convincing performance at his national broadcast at 1800 GMT.

Some financials found support amid hopes of a restructuring in the banking sector. Societe Generale gained 1.46 percent to 625, Cie Bancaire firmed 1.64 percent 743 and CCF rose 1.05 percent to 250.60.
Axa advanced 0.42 percent to 356.70. BNP was flat at 223.50.
